12. C1: deposits, withdrawals, signing. START only records and EXIT moves nothing. "EXIT unwinds into the wallet" is not done.
13. Header: not logos/logo-12.svg but a 6-path redraw of a 36-shape mark.

THE LOOK

16. Colours: spec #00ff88, #ff4444, #0a0e17, #0d1520; rendered #3DDC8A, #FF6B6B, #070B10, #0D141C. A washed-out green and a salmon EXIT in Inter 400. FIND and START are cyan; both are drawn green.
17. The step list's right column breaks word by word ("13,750 / USD / in / wstETH"), in Top 3 and Plan.

Not checked: Firefox, phone, clicking - and + (the API recomputes).

body.improvements:
Follow-up to the Agent Casino builds, written after a day of paper play (10 bots, 17 seats on finished Flash 1H/5H tables, coach on and off, Risk 1 and 10). Goals, not methods; the site's own look, colours and fonts. English, numbers before words.
1. A seat starts with its table: its clock, its daily allowance and its ROI begin at the table's start, not at Approve. Today a bot trades from Approve (table 35: approved 10:04, first round 10:05, table started 10:18), a round opened before the start and closed after it counts in the table's ROI and is missing from the owner's trade list, and a bot waiting for a table to fill uses up its 20 trades before the game begins.
2. A bot's owner sees "N trades left today" at the ask and at Approve, and a table that ends before the allowance resets is not offered to a bot with none left.
3. One lost round does not pause a bot: the stop loss is several stakes wide at every Risk level, not equal to the stake. When a bot is paused, the coach panel says so and until when (today the standings row shows PAUSED while the panel says "NEXUS COACH ON, no change").
4. At the ask the owner sees how often the bot trades ("about 2 trades an hour") and which table length suits it. Today 10 of 17 of our seats made no trade on a 1 H table, and a table where nothing happens is a dead game.
5. House seats are opponents that play: 15 of 45 house seats on our finished tables made no trade, and still ranked above a member who traded and lost.
6. A table with one member and house bots says so before Approve ("the pot is only yours"), or the house seats add to the pot. Today the member's prize is their own buy-in back whatever the bot does.
7. A seat that never traded is shown as such, not as the winner: at +0.00 % it ranks 1st or 2nd above bots that traded and lost and takes the buy-in back as a prize (tables 41, 42, 44, 46). The WINNER line names whoever takes the prize.
8. ET10 follows the result. Today a member gets the same 3 ET10 at rank 6 of 6 with -22.58 % as at rank 1 with +31.24 %. If it is a reward for taking part, the page says so.
9. A bot that plays two tables says so on both tables ("also plays table N, its settings are shared"), or each seat has its own settings. Today two coaches tune the same stop loss and neither table's log can explain the number (table 43's log ends at "stop loss 10 to 9" while the settings read 8).
10. The coach can loosen as well as tighten, and can change the trade size. Of 22 tunes on our tables, 16 tighten a stop loss and none loosens one or touches the size; one tightened after a +$26.77 run only because the rank went from 1 to 2. A tune follows the bot's own results, not a neighbour's.
11. At the end of a table one line says what the coach changed and what that did to the ROI; the owner can compare coach on against coach off across tables.
12. The coach makes no tune in the last minutes of a table, and each line says what it hopes to change (today "stop loss 5 to 4 %, rank 3 to 4" six minutes before the end, with no trade after it).
13. "nothing left to change inside the limits" names the limits, or is not shown (a tune follows two minutes later at tables 33 and 40). "tuned 8 min ago; no closed trade since" counts what the standings count (table 27: two rounds had closed after the tune).
14. The deal block, the "How it works" text and the "(1 day)" labels on a 1 H or 5 H table follow the table's real length.
15. "NEXUS TUNES" counts tunes, not checks that changed nothing.
16. After the owner moves Risk, the coach panel follows at once ("Risk reads 8") and the Changelog row says what moved ("Risk 5 to 8", not only "changed trade size, stop loss, take profit").
17. Lobby: "Live now" and "Open, starts when full" follow the length filter that is on.
18. Create a table offers the lengths people play (1 H, 5 H, 1 D), not only "Flash · 1 day".
19. A result header says what is paid and what waits ("3 ET10 waiting for treasury coverage" under "PAID OUT +3 ET10").
20. "1 won · 3 lost" adds the flat ones ("1 won · 3 lost · 1 flat") so it adds up to "5 closed".
21. The trade list shows when a round opened and when it closed, with headings, since the coach and the stop act on the close.
Done when:
[ ] 1-2 A seat's ROI, trades and allowance count from the table's start; "trades left today" shows at the ask and at Approve.
[ ] 3-5 No bot is paused by one loss at any Risk; a paused bot is named by the panel; the ask shows how often a bot trades; house seats trade.
[ ] 6-8 A one-member table says so before Approve; a no-trade seat is not the winner; ET10 follows the result or is labelled a reward.
[ ] 9-13 A shared bot says so on both tables; the coach loosens and resizes; the end-of-table line exists; no late tunes; the coach's sentences agree with the trades.
[ ] 14-21 The labels, counts, filters, lengths, paid/waiting header, won/lost/flat and the two times follow the table as above.

body.improvements:
New app, working name Pitch Cards, with one Profit Board for all of Cymetica. It sits in your normal page, under your header and above your chat bar. We supply the look and a few examples; the rest is yours to build your own way. Everything is at https://github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica/tree/ffdc39e854da4f7e94ec43a844eb855bcdeead95/outbox/pitch-cards: the working code (run python serve.py, open http://127.0.0.1:8802/pitch-cards), and in 1-build-it-better/ the pictures (1-entry, 2-swipe, 3-amount, 4-profit-board, 5-tags, 6-phone; "picture N" below) and motion.webm, the animation to match.
The idea: pitches come to every user on the web. Nexus plays the investor walking into a TV show like Dragons' Den: it brings an idea and wants our money. The user swipes left to pass or right to put money in, then follows how the deal does.
Why the Profit Board: today what makes money on Cymetica is shown in scattered places, each with its own format and measure: /events/universe/movers, /fund-optimizations, /leaderboard#cards_72h, /fund-performance, /themes/performance and more. Everyone is waiting for the day Cymetica is profitable, and users ask on Telegram whether anyone is making money here yet, but no single page answers that. The Profit Board is that page: whoever wonders if money can be made on Cymetica yet comes and looks. It shows absolutely every profitable thing from all of Cymetica, always up to date, and nothing at a loss.
MUST STAY AS DRAWN: the look of the entry screen and the swipe, with all the animation. Please build these from our pc.css, pc.js and images, not a redraw of your own.
1. Entry screen (picture 1): your header, Back and chat bar stay. Below them the app bar of /airdrop-farmer: logo, PITCH over CARDS, tabs as one segmented control, a hairline under it, in its 1240 px column. Then the headline "Nexus pitches. / You swipe. / Every result public." in Archivo Black with the last line green, on the column's left edge; the live card under Nexus's fingertip, PASS and INVEST under the card; Nexus in front, standing out past the column's right edge; the room behind, fading into your page background on every side.
2. Sizes do not grow with the window: headline 58 px, card 400 x 530, Nexus at 72% of the render. His finger stays on the card at every desktop size. layout() in pc.js does this.
3. Use scene.webp (5120 x 2880) and nexus.webp (1840 x 2320) at that resolution. Nexus is a separate cut-out in front of the card.
4. A new pitch arrives: a line of light wipes the card on from his fingertip, the big number runs up, the green line draws while the faint peer lines fade in behind it, the sentence types out word by word, his eyes flare. His eyes pulse the whole time.
5. A card holds five things: a label line, the result as the big number, what it is, the chart, one or two sentences in Nexus's voice.
6. Swipe (picture 2): the card follows the finger and tilts, INVEST or PASS fills it in its colour, past 110 px it goes. The buttons do the same.
7. Left: the card flies off and the next pitch arrives.
8. Right (picture 3): the card turns over to the same face with the big number now the amount, the chart still in view, chips $10 $25 $50 All, buttons Not now and Invest $25, under the same thumb.
9. Invest: the card slides right and behind Nexus, his eyes flare, the next pitch arrives.
10. Phone (picture 6): your header and chat bar stay, his face looks over the card, the same motion.
11. Profit Board look (pictures 4, 5): built from the table and tabs of your own /themes/performance, under "What would have made you money on Cymetica." Every kind of investment has its own coloured tag, in your palette. Columns: Up since start, Peak, and one Days column with two numbers, how many days old it is / the day of its life the peak came (47 / 45), over a line of its whole life with the peak marked on it. Numbers green; nothing red, because nothing at a loss is on it.
12. Your page background on every tab; only Pitches adds the room.
YOURS TO DECIDE: everything else. The mock only shows examples.
13. What Nexus presents: which ideas, when, how often, in what words. The two pitches in the mock are examples.
14. Profit Board categories and filters: you decide which come in. The tabs and tags in the mock (Pitches, Funds, Event cards, Company cards, 72h cards) are examples; add a tag and a colour for every further kind you list.
15. What counts as profitable, how a row is measured, how it stays up to date.
16. Credit, amounts, real money, fees and anything else behind the Invest button; the $100 in the mock is an example and investing there only moves counters on the page.
17. My deals: the five deals in the mock are examples, their amounts and days made up. Build it and everything else the drawings leave open your way, in the same look.
18. The numbers in the mock were read from your API on 2026-11-01 and not checked by us. They are there to fill the design, not as a claim about any product.
Done when:
[ ] 1-3 The entry screen looks like picture 1 at 1440 and 1920 px, inside your header and chat bar, sharp, with his finger on the card.
[ ] 4-9 The animation and swipe match motion.webm and pictures 2 and 3: light wipe, number, line, typed sentence, eyes, tilt, flip, card going behind him.
[ ] 10 The phone looks like picture 6.
[ ] Pitches reach every user on the web.
[ ] 11 The Profit Board looks like pictures 4 and 5, every kind with its own coloured tag, the Days column with its line.
[ ] One page holds every profitable thing from all of Cymetica, always up to date, nothing at a loss.
[ ] 12 Nothing overlaps.

body.improvements:
Gem Screener, Top Picks and the coin panel: what a reader needs to trust a pick before buying it, on the screen where they decide. No figure is computed differently and no gate changes.
Why: today a pick that had an $8.5M exploit nine months ago, or passes Liquid on exchange volume with 7% slip in its pool, reads the same as any other; and a near miss shows no figures until it is clicked.
MUST STAY AS DRAWN: the Watch out block, the Liquid row and the near-miss tooltip (pictures 1 and 4), in the site's fonts and palette.

1. Top Picks card: a pick with an exploit in the last year says so on the card, with the amount and the date, read from the same check the Guardians use. Picture 1: Meteora "Exploit in the last year: $1.5M, 17 Jan 2026". The panel and the Security guardian stay as they are.
2. Top Picks card, the $10K buy row: when the pool's slip is over 3%, the row shows the slip first and the volume under it, named for what it is. Picture 1: Dolomite "7% slip", under it "passes on $3.4M a day, all venues". At 3% or under the row stays as it is ("1.7% slip").
3. Top Picks card: a "Watch out" block between the gate rows and the Degen meter, carrying only that pick's own warnings: an exploit in the last year, not growing, dilution unknown. Red when it holds an exploit, otherwise cyan. No block when a pick has none. "The theme has lagged BTC" does not go in it, and stays where it is off the card. 4. In that block, "not growing" says why with the row's own figure: "Not growing: 30-day revenue is 20% of its best".
5. Coin panel, To holders, and the smiley's tooltip: where the last 30 days and the last 12 months differ, both are shown, in place of "None, no payouts, buybacks or burns found". Lido: "last 30 days 0% · 12 months 20%"; the smiley reads "Holders got 20% over 12 months, 0% in the last 30 days". Picture 2.

7. 9. The backtest line on Top Picks gives the date of the run and the days of forward record: "Backtest of the old gates, run 22 Sept: inconclusive. 18 days of forward record on these gates, first reading 12 Nov. A shortlist, not a signal."
10. Near misses: on hover or keyboard focus, a near miss shows the same card as a pick (the same gate rows, Watch out block and Degen meter), headed "Why it is not a pick" and "5 / 6 gates" in red, with the row of the gate it fails marked in red. ENGINE

3. "Dollar-only: the risk is the venue and the stablecoin itself" is false on the routes that lead. High #1 (+9.00%) matches Pendle Ecosystem High Yield USDC, about three weeks old, lending against PT-reUSD ($7.12M) and PT-USD3 ($4.82M). Medium #1 (+7.89%) matches Kamino Institutional Commodity Yield. Conservative #2 (+5.53%) matches RockawayX RWA USDC. The page never names the vault or market, only "Morpho Blue" or "Kamino Lend", so the user cannot tell which one or what it lends against.
4. "No savings dollar earns more than the loan costs" is false. stUSDS reads 6.03% by your rule; the Morpho stUSDS/USDC market borrows at 4.16%. 3x nets 9.78%, 22% from liquidation, about $35 a month at Sky's zero swap fee, $20 at 0.05% each way.
5. #3 is not the third best. OG #3 is $35.50 while WETH-USDT 0.3% on Uniswap V3 earns over $100 by your rule, and USDC-WETH 0.01% about $95-104. Medium and High #3 is the split at $21.72 while roxUSDCy reads 7.52%. If a top 3 is one per venue, the page has to say so.
6. Base has no route. routable_chains lists 16 of your 17 chains. Your Platforms tab lists 12 platforms on Base; Aave USDC reads 5.08% and Uniswap V3 WETH-USDC holds $150M at 17.94%.
7. "No audit on record" is the launch-date defect again: an empty DefiLlama field read as a failed check. Fluid Lending passes and Fluid DEX fails; SparkLend passes and Spark Savings fails; Curve passes and LlamaLend fails. Orca fails with 11 audit PDFs in orca-so/whirlpools/.audits, and Orca SOL-USDC at 48.96% is the best route the finders found outside your set. Circle CCTP passes "Audited" with the same empty field.
8. The Beefy note is wrong: USDC on Ethereum ($3.03M, 30-day 5.43%) and on Monad ($3.32M, 5.70%) pass its $3M test.
9. C1.1 stays open. It is in your review slot as asked, and the page says so, but this product still moves no money.

ON THE PAGE
10. Your fix for 17 cuts the text. "r info" on a step picks up .info { width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50% }. "Circle CCTP" and "$15,000 in wstETH" are cut, with a ring over them, on every CCTP and loop step, in both browsers.
11. The apex number does not fit: "+0.72%" is 60 wide in a 54-wide hex, dark text running onto a dark card.
12. On the risk cards a divider runs through "USDC lending · Kamino Lend · on 5,000 USDC".
13. Platforms: 13 of 41 names are cut at 1440 ("Morpho Bl", "Rocket Poo"), 3 at 2560.
14. End of EXIT: the mockup ends on a clean wallet screen. Yours adds the ring and DONE under the tree and progress panel. The ring sits behind the panel, the title scrolls off, and DONE touches the screen edge at 900.
15. Plan, on a loop (your /route fed into /top3 here): "wstETH slips 18.7% vs ETH" wraps to 4 lines and stretches the row.

Not checked: START and EXIT against your real API (answered in our browser, nothing sent).

The look and the motion are right, thank you: entry screen, swipe, flip and phone all match. Failing it on what is left:
1. C1, real money from day one, was accepted and is not built. Please name the ticket and the date for the human-reviewed build.
2. Pitches do not reach every user: the page has no link from anywhere yet. Please say what ends the freeze for it.
3. The Profit Board shows losers as up and misses a live fund: reports #289, #290, #291. Its 72h peak days are wrong on 2,774 rows: #292.
4. One bad reading draws the first pitch's chart flat: #293.
5. "Invest opens the product's own page" is on the page and it does not: Invest shows a link for 6 seconds. Open the page, or change the words.
6. Nexus does not write its pitches. The sentence is our mock's template word for word (pc.js line 81), the same one for every fund, and "Still climbing" sits on Molecular, down from +30.03 % to +15.8 % in five days. Our words were only examples (item 13). Nexus should reason for itself and write each pitch from that pitch's own numbers.
7. What is on the board and what Nexus pitches is our mock copied: the tabs, the tags and the bar for a pitch (8 weeks, 5 %, $10B, 7 days) are ours word for word. Our mock was only a proposal, and we cannot see into your platform the way you can (items 13-15). Please go through the whole platform yourselves and decide what belongs on the board and what Nexus pitches. For example, the theme baskets of /themes/performance, which the request itself names, have no place on the board, and 6,482 of its 6,854 rows are 72h cards.

body.improvements:
Cymetica Quest at /quest: one page that tells a visitor in five steps how to join the Quest, earn points and win up to 50,000 ET10 a month, and a plain file that tells an arriving AI agent the same.
Why: /quest answers 404 today. Season 1 is live (50,000 / 30,000 / 10,000 ET10, 100 points to qualify) but the only place it is explained is the season API; an owner or agent who hears of it has nowhere to start.
SOURCE: the pictures are shot from the finished page, complete with every file it needs, https://github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica/tree/main/outbox/quest-steps . HANDOVER.md there says how to run it (python serve.py 8800) and where each file goes: index.html, quest.css, quest.js, anim.js, outlines.js, pics/, clips/ (the six clips, mp4 and webm), scenes/tools.html, llms.txt (the agent file). Serve those files at /quest as they are; do not rebuild or restyle them. Change nothing in them: the prizes, the pool and the step 5 board are fixed on purpose, and the links are as written.
MUST STAY AS DRAWN: the first screen, the five steps and the two doors at the end (pictures 1 to 4), and the phone (picture 5), in the site's fonts and palette. The step 5 board is an example, its companies and points stay as drawn and are not read from any API; the prizes are fixed figures, not read from one either.

1. First screen: the headline, a green "Start a company" key, and a Monthly prizes board with the three prizes and the month's pool: 50,000 / 30,000 / 10,000 ET10 and 90,000, as drawn. Each figure lives in one place (QUEST in quest.js) and is used everywhere, so the board, the bar and the text never disagree. Picture 1.
2. A fixed top bar: the Quest mark, the five steps with the one on screen lit and a line that fills as you read, and "Up to 50,000 ET10 / month" from the same figure. Picture 1.
3. Step 1, Start an AI-native company: the company in two figures, 4 departments and 9 AI agents led by NEXUS, as the builder's own start gives them; one line that opens the Universe. Picture 2.
4. Step 2, Build your own products: the Build it Better pipeline as a short loop (an idea goes in; Spec, Design, Build, Security, Deploy, Hosting; a live product comes out, one of the products Build it Better has built); "Earn points when your products are used by other users or agents"; "Build it Better pipeline" opens /build-it-better. Picture 2.
5. Step 3, Get seen: the Promo Market (link) and your products on your own land in the Universe; each product named in the picture (Gem Screener, Agent Casino, Airdrop Farmer) opens its own page. Picture 3.
6. Step 4, Breed your own hero agent in Quant Lab: "Quant Lab" opens /company/app/experiments, "Agent Casino" opens its page, "Earn more points when those agents trade". Picture 3.
7. Step 5, Farm points, climb the leaderboard: the example leaderboard as drawn (six companies, their points, the three paid places with their ET10, your own company climbing it), "top 3 paid slots of the month", "Earn up to 50,000 ET10 every month". Picture 4.
8. Two doors at the end: "Start a company" opens /company/app/builder, "Explore the Universe" opens /company/app#universe. The green key is green at rest, not only on hover. Picture 4.
9. Every step has a short looping clip of the live product (the office, the Universe, Quant Lab, the Promo Market). A clip loads when its step is near and never blocks the page: the first load is under 2 MB, a poster shows until a clip plays, no loading screen, and nothing on the page moves under the mouse; only light changes.
10. Phone: one column, the headline and the green key first, the prizes under them (picture 5). Laptops down to 1280 px and a tablet on its side at 1024 px: nothing cut, nothing overlapping.
11. For agents, in the background: /quest/llms.txt (the file llms.txt in the folder is ready to publish; keep its figures in step with the season API), markdown in the style of /llms.txt, linked as the first entry of /llms.txt ("Join the Cymetica Quest"), from the page head as a link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown", and from /.well-known/agent.json.
12. What that file says: what the Quest is; this month's prizes and the points table exactly as the season API states them (what_counts), with the date they were read; how an agent takes part with calls that exist today (register a key, clone a bot on paper, fund it, turn trading on, report the result to its owner); what earns points for an agent's trades, as what_counts says it; and what only the owner can do (start a company at /company/app/builder, which needs a Pro plan and the ET10 fee). It states no step that does not work today.

Done when:
[ ] 1-2 /quest answers 200; the board reads 50,000 / 30,000 / 10,000 ET10 and a 90,000 pool, the bar and the headline 50,000, all from one place; they do not change when the season API does.
[ ] 3-4 The text and links are as written; each link opens the page named; the pipeline loop ends on a product that exists on the site.
[ ] 5-6 Each named product and Quant Lab and Agent Casino open their own pages.
[ ] 7 The board shows the example as drawn: six companies in rank order, the three paid places marked, your own company climbing it; nothing in it is read from a live source.
[ ] 8 Both doors open the pages named; the green key is green with the mouse away.
[ ] 9 First load under 2 MB at 1440 px; a clip plays when its step comes on screen at 10 Mbit/s; no layout moves under the mouse.
[ ] 10 At 390, 1024, 1280 and 1440 px nothing is cut or overlaps; on the phone the headline and green key come before the prizes.
[ ] 11 /quest/llms.txt answers 200 as text; /llms.txt lists it first; the page head and /.well-known/agent.json point to it.
[ ] 12 Every call and URL in the file works as written; its figures equal the season API's; a step that does not exist is not in it.
[ ] All of it looks like the pictures at 1440 and 1920 px.
